record.context_brief: three-eigenvalue Seidel matrices without regular graph
record.original_question: Do there exist Seidel matrices of order at least 14 with exactly three distinct eigenvalues whose switching class contains no regular graph?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.33. Do there exist any Seidel matrices of order at least 14 with precisely three distinct eigenvalues whose switching class does not contain a regular graph ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a symmetric $n\times n$ matrix with zero diagonal and off-diagonal entries in $\{-1,+1\}$; such a matrix is called a Seidel matrix. To every simple graph $\Gamma$ on $n$ vertices one associates the Seidel matrix $S(\Gamma)$ whose $(i,j)$-entry (for $i\neq j$) equals $-1$ if $i$ and $j$ are adjacent in $\Gamma$ and $+1$ otherwise. Two graphs $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$ on the same vertex set are called Seidel-switching equivalent if there exists a subset $U$ of the vertex set such that $\Gamma'$ is obtained from $\Gamma$ by complementing all edges between $U$ and its complement (and leaving all other adjacencies unchanged). The switching class of $\Gamma$ is the equivalence class under this relation; equivalently, it corresponds to the equivalence class of $S(\Gamma)$ under conjugation by signed diagonal $\pm 1$ matrices.

Question: Does there exist an integer $n \ge 14$ and a Seidel matrix $S$ of order $n$ such that $S$ has exactly three distinct eigenvalues and the switching class of (any graph corresponding to) $S$ contains no regular graph?
artifact.status_search_result: Known partial results: every Seidel matrix of odd order with precisely three distinct eigenvalues contains a regular (in fact strongly regular) graph in its switching class, and the same holds for all such matrices of order at most 12. Some sources indicate that examples (even an infinite family) of Seidel matrices with exactly three distinct eigenvalues whose switching class contains no regular graph have been pointed out in subsequent work (e.g. enumeration/classification work by Szöllősi and Östergård up to order 23, with a candidate at order 18), but the search did not yield a definitive, citable confirmation that the existence question for orders $\ge 14$ has been fully resolved. The status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Equiangular line systems and switching classes containing regular graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies when Seidel matrices with three distinct eigenvalues have a regular graph in their switching class; shows odd-order case always does.
status_evidence.claim: All Seidel matrices of odd order with precisely three distinct eigenvalues contain a strongly regular graph in their switching class.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Seidel matrices (Szöllősi–Östergård)
status_evidence.snippet: Classifies Seidel matrices with exactly three distinct eigenvalues for small orders and points out instances/families related to switching classes without regular graphs.
status_evidence.claim: Computational classification work addresses the existence question for small orders, with results suggesting candidates beyond order 12.
